components.name: Affix
components.summary: A bar that stays where the reader put it while the page scrolls past. The bar is held with position: sticky, so the browser keeps it in the flow and pins it to the edge of the scrollport — no scroll listener, no measuring, no JavaScript.

components.name: Border
components.summary: A frame of one semantic colour around a block of content. It says what state the content is in without adding a word to it.

components.name: Color
components.summary: The semantic colours of the mood, drawn as a readable palette. Every cell names the role it shows and the address of the value behind it.

components.name: Config Provider
components.summary: Element Plus's config provider is a Vue context: it hands the global size, the z-index, the locale and the namespace down to everything beneath it. A CSS-only library has no context to hand anything down, so this one is an attribute contract instead — a wrapper element carrying data-um-size and data-um-radius, and the library's own CSS answering to them. It sets the density and the radius mode of its subtree, and it says plainly that it cannot do the rest: there is no locale for it to set and no z-index for it to hand out.

components.name: Container
components.summary: A fixed width, centred block of content. The width is a step of the type size rather than a number of pixels, so a mood with larger type gets a larger container.

components.name: Icon
components.summary: The handful of marks a page needs most, drawn in CSS out of borders and pseudo-elements. The library ships no icon font, so every glyph here is a shape.

components.name: Layout
components.summary: The skeleton of a page: a header, a side column, the content and a footer. It draws the rules that separate them and leaves the surfaces to the page behind it.

components.name: Link
components.summary: A link, in one of the semantic colours. It is text, so it takes the text form of the colour and reads at 4.5:1 on the page, on an overlay and inside a container.

components.name: PageHeader
components.summary: The title of a page, the line that says what the page is about, and the actions that belong to it. The title is a real heading at the level the page asks for, so the document outline stays right however the header is styled.

components.name: Scrollbar
components.summary: A box that scrolls, with a scrollbar drawn in the mood's own colours instead of the platform's. The bar is a shape and a line, not a widget: there is no thumb to drag with a mouse, only a box that scrolls.

components.name: Space
components.summary: A run of things with the same space between them. The space is one gap on the container, not a margin on each child, so the last child carries no trailing space and the run wraps without a gap of its own.

components.name: Splitter
components.summary: Two panes with a divider between them. The divider is a line with a grip on it, and the grip says which way the thing can be moved. Moving it is the host's job: the library draws the shape and stops there.

components.name: Text
components.summary: A run of inline text in one of the library's colours. It is the smallest atom of the type system: no box, no border, only the words and the colour they are written in. The blocks a page is written in are the typography component; this is the coloured run inside one of them.

components.name: Typography
components.element: div, h1, h2, p, span, a, blockquote
components.summary: The set of text styles a page is written in: a title, a subtitle, a paragraph, supporting text, a link and a quote. The library paints the sizes, the colours and the leading; the words and the heading levels are the host's.

components.name: Autocomplete
components.summary: A text field that offers values while the reader types. The suggestions live in a native <datalist>, so the browser filters them, the arrow keys walk them and the popup opens without a line of script.

components.name: Button
components.summary: An action the user takes. The one component every interface needs, and the one that has to look right in thirty-two different moods.

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: A box that either is ticked or is not, for choosing one or many things out of a list. The tick is a shape drawn in CSS, not a character.

components.name: Checkbox Group
components.summary: A set of checkboxes that share one name and belong to one field. The group is a fieldset, so the browser groups the boxes for the form and for the screen reader.

components.name: Color Picker
components.summary: A colour in three parts: the platform's own colour button, a row of palette chips the reader can pick from, and the hexadecimal value written out. The chips are a real radio group, so the choice is in the tab order and the browser announces it.

components.name: Color Picker Panel
components.summary: The panel a colour picker drops: the colours the host has predefined, a choice among the theme's own named colours, and the hexadecimal value written out. Every swatch is a real radio, so the choice is in the tab order and the browser announces it.

components.name: Date Picker
components.summary: A field for a date. It is a real <input type="date"> inside a box the library draws, so the browser validates the date, the arrow keys walk through it and the reader's own calendar opens it.

components.name: Date Picker Panel
components.summary: The month panel a date picker drops: the month and its navigation, the week grid, and the two actions in the footer. The panel does not keep a month, so the host owns the month and the buttons that change it.

components.name: Date Time Picker
components.summary: A field for a date and a time together. It is a real <input type="datetime-local"> inside a box the library draws, so the browser validates both halves, the arrow keys walk the segments and the reader's own calendar opens it.

components.name: Field
components.summary: The scaffolding around a control: a label, the control itself, and a line of text that says what to do next. It owns the spacing, so a form does not have to.

components.name: Input / Textarea / Select
components.nameZh: 输入框 / 文本域 / 选择器
components.summary: The three text controls a form is mostly made of: a single-line input, a multi-line textarea and a native select. One stylesheet gives all three the same border, focus ring and disabled treatment, so a form reads as one form.

components.name: Input Number
components.summary: A field for a number, with a pair of buttons that step it up and down. The buttons are real buttons, so they are in the tab order and the browser announces them; the browser's own spin buttons are taken away so there is only one pair.

components.name: Input OTP
components.summary: A row of one-character fields for a code the reader has been sent. Each box is a real input that holds one character, so the browser's own keyboard, autofill and password manager all still apply to it.

components.name: Input Tag
components.summary: A field that holds the tags already chosen, and an empty place to type the next one. Removing a tag needs a script; the shapes of the tag and of its remove button do not.

components.name: Mention
components.summary: A field with a list of people under it. The reader types, the host decides which names to offer, and each name is a button that carries an avatar slot and an @name.

components.name: Radio
components.summary: A round control for choosing exactly one option out of a set. Radios that share a name form a group, and the browser owns the exclusivity.

components.name: Radio Group
components.summary: A set of radios that share one name and belong to one field. The group is a fieldset, so the browser groups the circles for the form and for the screen reader.

components.name: Rate
components.summary: A row of stars the reader sets by choosing one. The stars are real radio buttons under a drawn shape, so the value is the browser's own value and the group is the browser's own group.

components.name: Slider
components.summary: A number picked by sliding along a track. It is a native range input, so the drag, the steps and the value are the platform's.

components.name: Switch
components.summary: A binary setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped. The visible switch is drawn by the library; the control underneath it is a real checkbox.

components.name: Time Picker
components.summary: A field for a time of day. It is a real <input type="time"> inside a box the library draws, so the browser validates the hour, the arrow keys walk the segments and the reader's own clock opens it.

components.name: Time Select
components.summary: A choice of time of day, as a native <select>. The option list is the platform's own, so the reader gets the system's own picker and its keyboard behaviour; the library draws the field and the arrow around it.

components.name: Tree Select
components.summary: A tree you pick a leaf from. The branches are disclosures, so the browser opens and closes them, and the leaf that is picked is a real radio, so the browser keeps exactly one of them picked.

components.name: Upload
components.summary: A file input and the list of the files that were chosen. The input is a real one, so the browser's own dialog opens and the files are chosen with the browser's own picker.

components.name: Virtual Select
components.summary: A long list of choices that the browser only lays out near the viewport. The rows far away are skipped, and the browser is told how tall such a row is, so the scrollbar is right without every row being built.

components.name: Avatar
components.summary: A small picture of a person. It takes a photo, a pair of initials or an icon, and it keeps the shape of whichever mood it is in.

components.name: Badge
components.summary: A small marker that counts or names a state, attached to something else. It comes in a solid fill and a soft tint, so a page can let what matters come forward and the rest recede.

components.name: Calendar
components.summary: One month laid out as a seven-column grid. It draws the month and marks the days; which month to show is the host's business, because a grid cannot know which months exist.

components.name: Card
components.summary: A surface that groups one thing: a title, a body, a footer. Its border, radius, shadow and fill all come from the mood, so one card reads correctly in all thirty-two of them.

components.name: Carousel
components.summary: Slides the reader scrolls through, with a button at each end of a slide that moves to the neighbouring one. The track is a real scroller, so the browser does the scrolling and the snapping.

components.name: Cascader
components.summary: Options in levels, opened one level at a time. Every level is a disclosure, so the browser does the opening and the closing and the state survives a reload.

components.name: Collapse
components.summary: A panel that opens and closes. It is a real disclosure, so the browser does the opening and the closing and the state survives a reload.

components.name: Descriptions
components.summary: The facts about one thing, as label and value pairs. It is a definition list, so a screen reader announces each label before the value it belongs to.

components.name: Empty
components.summary: What a screen shows when there is nothing to show. It states the fact, and when there is a way out of it, it says what that way is.

components.name: Image
components.summary: A frame for a picture: it holds the space the picture will take, shows a placeholder while there is none, and decides how the picture fills that space.

components.name: Infinite Scroll
components.summary: A feed the reader can scroll a long way through, and a sentinel at the end of it that says what comes next. The library cannot load anything: it provides the container, the skipped layout and the sentinel, and the host decides what to load.

components.name: Progress
components.summary: How much of something is done. The bar is a groove with a fill inside it, and the fill takes its width from the host.

components.name: Result
components.summary: The end of a flow: one statement of what happened, a line of explanation, and the way out. It is the whole answer on one screen, not a toast that disappears.

components.name: Segmented
components.summary: A row of choices that show which one is picked, drawn as radios under a shared frame. The browser keeps the selection, so the group behaves like the radio group it is.

components.name: Skeleton
components.summary: The shape of content that has not arrived yet. Three placeholder shapes and, if the motion is welcome, a shimmer over them.

components.name: Statistic
components.summary: One number with the name of what it counts. The number is the largest thing on the block and everything else is sized around it.

components.name: Table
components.element: table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, div
components.summary: Rows of records in columns. It is a real table, so the column names travel with the cells and a screen reader can read a row across.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: A label for one piece of data — a category, a state, a filter. The outlined member of the chip family, so it can sit beside a filled badge without either of them winning.

components.name: Timeline
components.summary: What happened, in order. An ordered list with a rail down one side and a dot at each entry, so the order is in the structure and not only in the picture.

components.name: Tour
components.summary: A walkthrough that points at one thing on the page and says what to do with it. The ring is the thing being pointed at, the card is what the tour says, and the dots are how far along the walkthrough is. Moving from one step to the next is the host's job.

components.name: Transfer
components.summary: Two lists side by side with a button between them: what is available on one side, what has been chosen on the other. The whole thing is a form, so the move is a submission.

components.name: Tree
components.summary: Things inside things. Every branch is a disclosure, so the browser opens and closes it and the state survives a reload.

components.name: Virtualized Table
components.summary: A long table the browser is not asked to lay out in full. The rows far from the viewport are skipped and given a placeholder size, so the cost of the list is what is near it.

components.name: Virtualized Tree
components.summary: A tree so large that the browser is asked to lay out only the branches near the reader. Every branch is still a disclosure, so the browser opens and closes it and the state survives a reload.

components.name: Anchor
components.summary: A column of links to the sections of the page, with a rule down the side so the reader can see that they are a list of places rather than a list of links. The section being read is marked with aria-current, because CSS cannot work out what is on screen.

components.name: Backtop
components.summary: A round button that takes the reader back to the top of the page. It is a link to a fragment, so it works with the keyboard alone and needs no scroll listener to appear — it is simply there.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.summary: The path to the page you are on, as a list of links. The separators between the steps are drawn by the stylesheet, not written into the markup as characters.

components.name: Dropdown
components.summary: A row of actions that stays out of the way until it is wanted. The trigger is a <summary>, so the panel opens and closes with the browser's own disclosure behaviour.

components.name: Menu
components.summary: A list of places to go, with groups that fold away. The groups are <details> elements, so the browser opens and closes them and keeps them open across a reload.

components.name: Pagination
components.element: nav, ul, li, a, button, input
components.summary: The pages of a long list, with the previous and next arrows at either end and the current page filled in. The arrows are chevrons drawn from two borders.

components.name: Steps
components.summary: The order of a job, one step per entry, with the step you are on picked out and the steps already done marked as finished.

components.name: Tabs
components.summary: One row of tabs over several panels of content. The tabs are radio inputs, so the browser keeps the selection, the focus and the arrow keys without a line of script.

components.name: Alert
components.summary: A message that stays in the page and says what the reader has to know: the run failed, the quota is nearly gone, the sync is through. The variant colours the border and the mark, not the text.

components.name: Dialog
components.summary: A panel that asks the reader something, written as a <dialog>. It is shown the way a dialog is shown without JavaScript — open in the markup — and it is closed the way the browser closes one: the close button submits the form around it, and the form's method is dialog.

components.name: Drawer
components.summary: A panel that slides out from the edge of the page: a side panel with a title, a body and a row of actions. It is held against the edge with fixed positioning, so it stays put while the page moves behind it.

components.name: Loading
components.summary: A ring that turns while the library waits for something. The ring is two borders with one side left out, and the turn is a keyframe, so it needs neither a timer nor a script.

components.name: Message
components.summary: A short bar that tells the reader what just happened. Element Plus's message is a function that paints the bar and takes it away again; here the bar is a container, and the host decides whether it is on the page.

components.name: Message Box
components.element: dialog, form, h2, div, button, span
components.summary: The narrow, centred box that asks the reader to confirm: a title, a message, and a pair of buttons, with an icon that carries the type. It is written as a <dialog> with a form around it, so the browser's own close is the one that closes it — the buttons are submits inside a form whose method is dialog, and the library installs no listener anywhere.

components.name: Notification
components.summary: A card that reports something the reader did not ask about — a deployment finished, a certificate was renewed. It is wider than a message, and it carries a heading of its own.

components.name: Popconfirm
components.summary: A bubble that asks before it acts. It hangs off a trigger, and it holds a question and the two real buttons that answer it: confirm and cancel.

components.name: Popover
components.summary: A card that floats next to a trigger and holds more than a note: a heading, a body and a row of actions. The trigger is a <summary>, so the card opens and closes with the browser's own disclosure behaviour.

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: A short note that appears when the reader points at a word or tabs to it. The bubble is drawn by the stylesheet and placed with absolute positioning; the trigger is a real button, so the keyboard opens it as well as the pointer.

components.name: Divider
components.summary: A rule between two things. It can carry a label in the middle, drop the rules and keep the label, or stand up as a vertical rule.

components.name: Watermark
components.summary: A layer of the same word, repeated across a box, to say that what is underneath is a copy. The word is real text in the markup, tiled by the browser rather than baked into a picture.
